map.按泥料查询素烧与釉烧的推荐温度区间及保温时长，作为装窑烧制的参数依据。: Look up the recommended temperature range and hold time for the bisque and glaze firings by clay body, as the basis for kiln loading and firing.
map.对比不同泥料的烧成窗口，判断某釉料是否与坯体烧成温度匹配。: Compare the firing windows of different clay bodies to judge whether a glaze matches the firing temperature of the body.
map.按保温时长安排高温段的恒温控制，确保坯体或釉面充分反应。: Arrange constant-temperature control over the high-temperature segment according to the hold time so the body or glaze reacts fully.
map.：素烧/釉烧温度与保温：陶土（低温陶）800–950℃ / 980–1050℃: Bisque and glaze temperatures with holds: earthenware (low fire) 800-950℃ / 980-1050℃ / 20-30 min; stoneware clay (mid fire) 900-1000℃ / 1180-1240℃ / 30-45 min; kaolin (high fire porcelain) 900-980℃ / 1260-1320℃ / 40-60 min; purple clay 1000-1100℃ / 1120-1180℃ / 20-30 min; bone china 900-1000℃ / 1220-1280℃ / 30-40 min. The glaze firing temperature should be slightly below the limit of the body, and the hold lets the glaze melt fully.
map.：烧制高岭土瓷器：素烧取 950℃（区间 900–980 中值）保温 20–30: Firing kaolin porcelain: bisque at 950°C (the midpoint of 900-980) held 20-30 min so the body sets and gains enough strength for glazing; the glaze firing rises to 1300°C (1260-1320) held 50 min so the glaze fully vitrifies. If the glaze matures at 1200℃ it does not suit this body and stoneware clay should be chosen instead.
map.素烧温度为什么要低于釉烧？: Why is the bisque temperature lower than the glaze firing?
map.素烧目的是定型、脱水并产生一定孔隙以便吸釉，温度过高坯体过于致密反而不易挂釉；釉: The bisque firing sets the shape, removes water and creates some porosity so the glaze can be absorbed; too high a temperature makes the body too dense and hard to glaze, while the glaze firing needs high temperature so the glaze melts and vitrifies.
map.保温时间怎么影响成品？: How does the hold time affect the finished piece?
map.保温不足釉面未完全流平会有针孔、橘釉；过长则可能流釉粘底或坯体过烧变形，一般高温: If the hold is too short the glaze surface will not flow flat and pinholes or orange peel appear; too long and the glaze may run and stick to the kiln shelf or the body may be overfired and deform. High-fire porcelain generally needs 40-60 min while low-fire earthenware needs 20-30 min.
